title: Checking a part out and back in

steps.title: Start on Files
steps.body: Everything a project stores hangs off this tab — Drive, GitHub, and the Vault. Open it.

steps.title: The Vault is the third source
steps.body: Drive holds documents, GitHub holds code, the Vault holds parts. Open it.

steps.title: Parts, not files
steps.body: Every item here has one current version and every version before it. The Vault is a record of a part over time, not a folder you drop files into.

steps.title: Open this bracket
steps.body: Click the item to see its history.

steps.title: Three versions, newest first
steps.body: Each one records who uploaded it and why. Nothing is ever overwritten — the old revision is still there, it just stopped being current.

steps.title: Check it out
steps.body: From now until you check it back in, it's locked to you — and everyone can see that.

steps.title: Notice the lock, and your name on it
steps.body: That visibility is the entire mechanism. Check-out doesn't stop anyone by force — it makes the fact that you're mid-edit impossible to miss.

steps.title: Upload a new version
steps.body: Anything will do here. On a real part this is where your changed model goes.

steps.title: Four now
steps.body: The old one didn't go anywhere — it just stopped being current. That is what makes "go back to what we had last week" a real option rather than a hope.

steps.title: Check it back in, then open the BOM
steps.body: Check-in is the end of the edit, not a separate chore. Then open the BOM: this is what tells you what your change just touched.
